Technology stocks were finishing solidly on positive ground Thursday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 adding over 0.6% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a more than 0.5% gain.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ iQIYI Inc. ( IQ ) jumped out to a new, all-time high on Thursday, climbing over 14% to $39.74 a share, after the Chinese online entertainment company said it added several artificial-intelligence experts to its board of directors. Haifeng Wang, a senior vice president at Baidu ( BIDU ) as well the general manager of the AI group at the internet-search company, was named to the IQIYI board, effective Thursday. Also new to the board Thursday is Jane Jie Sun, CEO at Ctrip, an online travel broker, while Herman Yu was named chairman of the board's compensation committee replacing Qi Lu, who resigned from the board. Separately, IQIYI said it has begun an AI-programming competition focused on video-based multimodal biometric recognition. Between 200 to 1,000 teams from colleges and universities throughout China are expected to participate in the Celebrity Video Identification Challenge, which is being held in partnership with the Chinese Conference on Pattern Recognition and Computer Vision.
In other sector news:
+ Microsoft ( MSFT ) advanced Thursday, rising over 1% to climb within 66 cents of its 52-week high of $102.69 a share, following reports it is developing a technology platform that would do away with cashiers and checkout lines at retail stores and putting it in direct competition with Amazon's ( AMZN ) automated grocery shop. The software and hardware giant already has demonstrated the technology to several international retailers and is now looking to collaborate with Walmart ( WMT ), people familiar with the matter told Reuters. It was not clear, however, how soon Microsoft would deploy its automated checkout service, if at all, with the company Thursday telling Reuters it "does not comment on rumors or market speculation."
- Asure Software (ASUR) retreated Thursday, falling as much as 7%, after the workplace management software firm priced a $35 million public offering of 2 million shares of its common stock at $17.50 apiece, or about 5.4% under Wednesday's closing price. iSystems Holdings sold another 500,000 Asure shares in a concurrent secondary offering, pocketing $8.75 million in gross proceeds. Asure also provided underwriters with a 30-day option to buy up to 375,000 shares to cover potential overallotments. After first paying underwriter discounts and other offering expenses, the company expects to use the net proceeds to acquire or invest in complementary businesses, assets or technologies.
- Cision (CISN) was more than 7% lower on Thursday after the public relations and media distribution software firm late Wednesday disclosed plans for a secondary offering of 12 million shares. The selling sharesholders - Canyon Partners Ltd along with board members Mark Fin and L Dyson Dryden - also issued a 30-day option to the underwriters to buy up to 1.8 million additional shares to cover potential over-allotments.
